dot%20products%2C%20checks%20it%20on%20motions%20with%20known%20answers%2C%20and%20applies%20it%20to%20a%20forearm%2C%20a%20pendulum%20and%20the%20shank%20of%20a%20person%20walking.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Read%20it%20in%20order%20and%20run%20each%20cell%20as%20you%20reach%20it.%20Where%20you%20find%20a%20**Challenge**%20or%20a%20set%20of%20**Guiding%20questions**%2C%20stop%20and%20answer%20on%20a%20scratchpad%20before%20moving%20on.%20Several%20of%20them%20ask%20you%20to%20predict%20a%20number%20*before*%20the%20code%20prints%20it.%20Make%20the%20prediction%3B%20a%20wrong%20guess%20that%20the%20code%20then%20corrects%20teaches%20more%20than%20a%20right%20one.%20The%20**Exercises**%20come%20with%20collapsed%20solutions%3A%20open%20one%20only%20after%20you%20have%20tried%20the%20exercise%20yourself.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20You%20will%20need%20the%20planar%20angular%20velocity%20and%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%24%20from%20%5BKinematics%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_of_rigid_body.py)%2C%20rotation%20matrices%20and%20Cardan%20angles%20from%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_3d.py)%2C%20and%20a%20basis%20attached%20to%20a%20segment%2C%20built%20from%20markers%20as%20in%20%5BFrame%20of%20reference%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Freference_frame.py).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Before%20you%20begin%2C%20pick%20up%20a%20pen.%20Spin%20it%20about%20its%20long%20axis%20with%20your%20fingers%20while%20you%20swing%20your%20arm%20in%20an%20arc.%20At%20any%20one%20instant%2C%20is%20there%20a%20single%20line%20about%20which%20the%20pen%20is%20rotating%3F%20Or%20two%20rotations%20going%20on%20at%20once%3F%20Write%20down%20your%20answer%3B%20the%20checkpoint%20questions%20ask%20you%20to%20come%20back%20to%20it.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20How%20fast%20is%20the%20shank%20turning%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_3d.py)%2C%20the%20orientation%20of%20the%20right%20shank%20during%20a%20stride%20was%20described%20by%20three%20Cardan%20angles.%20The%20largest%20of%20them%2C%20%24%5Cgamma%24%2C%20the%20inclination%20of%20the%20shank%20in%20the%20sagittal%20plane%2C%20goes%20from%20about%20%24-65%5E%5Ccirc%24%20to%20%24%2B36%5E%5Ccirc%24%20during%20the%20stride%2C%20and%20in%20late%20swing%20it%20changes%20at%20almost%20%24380%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs.%20The%20other%20two%20angles%20change%20too%2C%20by%20tens%20of%20degrees%2C%20while%20the%20shank%20swings.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20So%20how%20fast%20is%20the%20shank%20turning%3F%20Is%20it%20%24380%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs%3F%20Is%20the%20angular%20velocity%20a%20vector%20with%20the%20three%20angle%20rates%20as%20its%20components%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%200.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20In%20a%20plane%2C%20the%20angular%20velocity%20is%20the%20derivative%20of%20the%20angle.%20Why%20might%20that%20stop%20being%20true%20when%20there%20are%20three%20angles%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20same%20orientations%20described%20with%20another%20Cardan%20sequence%20give%20different%20angles%2C%20and%20so%20different%20angle%20rates.%20Should%20two%20people%20using%20different%20sequences%20get%20different%20angular%20velocities%20for%20the%20same%20shank%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20angular%20velocity%20is%20a%20vector.%20What%20would%20its%20direction%20mean%20physically%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20 %2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_2d.py)%20and%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_3d.py)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20vector%20in%20the%20direction%20of%20the%20axis%20of%20rotation%20is%20a%20vector%20that%20does%20not%20change%20after%20the%20rotation.%20That%20is%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%5C%2C%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20vector%20is%20the%20eigenvector%20of%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%24%20with%20eigenvalue%20equal%20to%20one.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Below%2C%20the%20yellow%20arrow%20shows%20the%20axis%20of%20rotation%20between%20the%20reference%20frame%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bi%7D%7D%2C%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bj%7D%7D%2C%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bk%7D%7D%24%20(coloured%20arrows)%20and%20the%20reference%20frame%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%2C%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%2C%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%24%20(black%20arrows)%2C%20obtained%20by%20rotating%20the%20first%20one%20by%20%24%5Cgamma%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%2C%20then%20by%20%24%5Calpha%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20then%20by%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%2C%20all%20about%20the%20fixed%20axes%20of%20the%20laboratory.%20Use%20the%20sliders%20to%20change%20the%20angles.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(sym)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_a%2C%20_b%2C%20_g%20%3D%20sym.symbols(%22alpha%2C%20beta%2C%20gamma%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Elemental%20rotation%20matrices%20of%20xyz%20in%20relation%20to%20XYZ%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_RX%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20sym.cos(_a)%2C%20-sym.sin(_a)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20sym.sin(_a)%2C%20sym.cos(_a)%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_RY%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5Bsym.cos(_b)%2C%200%2C%20sym.sin(_b)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B-sym.sin( 0if%20relative.is_absolute()%20or%20%22..%22%20in%20relative.parts%20or%20%22%5C%5C%22%20in%20str(path)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20ValueError(%22Use%20a%20repository-relative%20path%20such%20as%20data%2Fwalk.trc%22)%0A%20%20%20%20location%20%3D%20mo.notebook_dir()%0A%20%20%20%20if%20location%20is%20not%20None%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20directory%20%3D%20Path(location).resolve()%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20for%20base%20in%20(directory%2C%20*directory.parents)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20local%20%3D%20base.joinpath(*relative.parts)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20local.is_file()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20local%0A%20%20%20%20url%20%3D%20base_url.rstrip(%22%2F%22)%20%2B%20%22%2F%22%20%2B%20quote(relative.as_posix()%2C%20safe%3D%22%2F%22)%0A%20%20%20%20key%20%3D%20hashlib.sha256(base_url.rstrip(%22%2F%22).encode()).hexdigest()%5B%3A16%5D%0A%20%20%20%20cached%20%3D%20(Path(tempfile.gettempdir())%20%2F%20%22bmc-notebooks-v2%22%20%2F%20key).joinpath(*relative.parts)%0A%20%20%20%20if%20not%20cached.is_file()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20response%20%3D%20urllib3.request(%22GET%22%2C%20url%2C%20timeout%3D30.0%2C%20retries%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20response.status%20!%3D%20200%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20OSError(f%22Cannot%20load%20%7Bpath%7D%3A%20HTTP%20%7Bresponse.status%7D%20from%20%7Burl%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20cached.parent.mkdir(parents%3DTrue%2C%20exist_ok%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20with%20tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir%3Dcached.parent%2C%20delete%3DFalse)%20as%20download%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20temporary%20%3D%20Path(download.name)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20download.write(response.data)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20try%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20temporary.replace(cached)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20finally%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20temporary.unlink(missing_ok%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20cached%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20sys%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_functions%20%3D%20%5Brepo_file(f%22functions%2F%7B_m%7D.py%22)%20for%20_m%20in%20(%22CCSbasis%22%2C%20%22read_trc%22)%5D%0A%20%20%20%20sys.path.insert(0%2C%20str(_functions%5B0%5D.parent))%20%20%23%20add%20to%20pythonpath%0A%20%20%20%20from%20CCSbasis%20import%20CCSbasis%0A%20%20%20%20from%20read_trc%20import%20read_trc%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20CCSbasis%2C%20read_trc%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(CCSbasis%2C%20alpha_slider%2C%20beta_slider%2C%20gamma_slider%2C%20np%2C%20rotation_matrix)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_R%20%3D%20rotation_matrix(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20np.radians(alpha_slider.value)%2C%20np.radians(beta_slider.value)%2C%20np.radians(gamma_slider.value)%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_e1%20%3D%20np.array(%5B%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_e2%20%3D%20np.array(%5B%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_e3%20%3D%20np.array(%5B%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%5D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_basis%20%3D%20np.vstack((_e1%2C%20_e2%2C%20_e3))%0A%20%20%20%20_basis_rot%20%3D%20_R%20%40%20_basis%0A%20%20%20%20_lv%2C%20_v%20%3D%20np.linalg.eig(_R)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Eigenvalues%20of%20R%3A%22%2C%20_lv.round(4))%0A%20%20%20%20if%20np.isclose(_lv%2C%201).sum()%20%3D%3D%203%3A%20%20%23%20no%20rotation%3A%20every%20direction%20is%20unchanged%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(%22No%20rotation%3A%20R%20is%20the%20identity%20matrix%2C%20and%20there%20is%20no%20axis%20to%20find.%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ccs%20%3D%20CCSbasis(Oijk%3Dnp.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%200%5D)%2C%20Oxyz%3Dnp.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%200%5D)%2C%20ijk%3D_basis.T%2C%20xyz%3D_basis_rot.T)%0A%20%20%20%20else%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_axis_of_rotation%20%3D%20%5Bnp.real(np.squeeze(_v%5B%3A%2C%20np.isclose(_lv%2C%201)%5D))%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(%22Axis%20of%20rotation%20(eigenvector%20of%20R%20with%20eigenvalue%201)%3A%22%2C%20_axis_of_rotation%5B0%5D.round(4))%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ccs%20%3D%20CCSbasis(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Oijk%3Dnp.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%200%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Oxyz%3Dnp.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%200%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ijk%3D_basis.T%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20xyz%3D_basis_rot.T%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20vector%3DTrue%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20point%3D_axis_of_rotation%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20With%20the%20default%20angles%2C%20a%20rotation%20of%20%2445%5E%5Ccirc%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20alone%2C%20the%20axis%20is%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20itself%2C%20%24%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%24.%20Try%20the%20sliders%3A%20whatever%20the%20three%20angles%2C%20the%20yellow%20arrow%20is%20a%20single%20line.%20Notice%20also%20the%20other%20two%20eigenvalues%3A%20they%20are%20complex.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%201.**%20Show%20that%20a%20rotation%20by%20an%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20has%20the%20eigenvalues%20%241%24%20and%20%24%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20%5Cpm%20i%5Csin%5Ctheta%24%2C%20and%20check%20them%20against%20the%20eigenvalues%20printed%20for%20the%20default%20%2445%5E%5Ccirc%24.%20Then%20use%20the%20fact%20that%20the%20trace%20of%20a%20matrix%20is%20the%20sum%20of%20its%20eigenvalues%20to%20find%20%24%5Coperatorname%7Btr%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%24%20in%20terms%20of%20%24%5Ctheta%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%201%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20a%20rotation%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%2C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20-%20%5Clambda%5Cmathbf%7BI%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Clambda%20%26%20-%5Csin%5Ctheta%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%20%5Csin%5Ctheta%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Clambda%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200%20%26%201%20-%20%5Clambda%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdet(%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20-%20%5Clambda%5Cmathbf%7BI%7D)%20%3D%20(1%20-%20%5Clambda)%5Cleft%5B(%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Clambda)%5E2%20%2B%20%5Csin%5E2%5Ctheta%5Cright%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20determinant%20is%20zero%20for%20%24%5Clambda%20%3D%201%24%20(the%20axis)%20and%20for%20%24(%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Clambda)%5E2%20%3D%20-%5Csin%5E2%5Ctheta%24%2C%20that%20is%2C%20%24%5Clambda%20%3D%20%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20%5Cpm%20i%5Csin%5Ctheta%20%3D%20e%5E%7B%5Cpm%20i%5Ctheta%7D%24.%20For%20%24%5Ctheta%20%3D%2045%5E%5Ccirc%24%20that%20is%20%240.7071%20%5Cpm%200.7071i%24%2C%20as%20printed.%20Only%20directions%20along%20the%20axis%20are%20left%20unchanged%3B%20no%20other%20real%20direction%20is.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20trace%20is%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20eigenvalues%2C%20so%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Coperatorname%7Btr%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20%3D%201%20%2B%20e%5E%7Bi%5Ctheta%7D%20%2B%20e%5E%7B-i%5Ctheta%7D%20%3D%201%20%2B%202%5Ccos%5Ctheta%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Every%20rotation%20about%20any%20axis%20is%20a%20rotation%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20written%20in%20another%20basis%2C%20and%20a%20change%20of%20basis%20does%20not%20change%20the%20eigenvalues%2C%20so%20this%20holds%20for%20every%20rotation%20matrix.%20It%20is%20the%20formula%20used%20for%20the%20angle%20in%20the%20next%20cell.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20eigenvector%20gives%20the%20line%20of%20the%20axis%2C%20but%20not%20which%20way%20along%20it%20the%20body%20turned%3A%20%24-%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%24%20is%20an%20eigenvector%20as%20well%2C%20and%20NumPy%20may%20return%20either.%20To%20get%20a%20direction%20and%20an%20angle%20that%20belong%20together%2C%20use%20the%20matrix%20itself.%20The%20angle%20comes%20from%20the%20trace%2C%20and%20the%20axis%2C%20pointing%20so%20that%20the%20rotation%20is%20counterclockwise%20by%20the%20right-hand%20rule%2C%20from%20the%20antisymmetric%20part%20of%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%24%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ctheta%20%3D%20%5Carccos%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7B%5Coperatorname%7Btr%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20-%201%7D%7B2%7D%5Cright)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bu%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%5Csin%5Ctheta%7D%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20R_%7B32%7D%20-%20R_%7B23%7D%20%5C%5C%20R_%7B13%7D%20-%20R_%7B31%7D%20%5C%5C%20R_%7B21%7D%20-%20R_%7B12%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20valid%20for%20%240%20%3C%20%5Ctheta%20%3C%20180%5E%5Ccirc%24.%20Conversely%2C%20Rodrigues'%20formula%20builds%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20from%20an%20axis%20and%20an%20angle.%20Here%20are%20both%2C%20and%20an%20elemental%20rotation%20about%20one%20of%20the%20fixed%20axes%2C%20as%20reusable%20functions%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20axis_angle(R)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Axis%20(versor)%20and%20angle%20%5Bdegrees%5D%20of%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20R%2C%20for%200%20%3C%20angle%20%3C%20180.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20R%20%3D%20np.asarray(R%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)%0A%20%20%20%20theta%20%3D%20np.arccos(np.clip((np.trace(R)%20-%201)%20%2F%202%2C%20-1%2C%201))%0A%20%20%20%20u%20%3D%20np.array(%5BR%5B2%2C%201%5D%20-%20R%5B1%2C%202%5D%2C%20R%5B0%2C%202%5D%20-%20R%5B2%2C%200%5D%2C%20R%5B1%2C%200%5D%20-%20R%5B0%2C%201%5D%5D)%20%2F%20(2%20*%20np.sin(theta))%0A%20%20%20%20return%20u%2C%20np.degrees(theta)%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20rodrigues(u%2C%20angle)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Rotation%20matrix%20for%20a%20rotation%20by%20%60angle%60%20%5Brad%5D%20about%20the%20axis%20%60u%60.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20u%20%3D%20np.asarray(u%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(u)%0A%20%20%20%20K%20%3D%20np.array(%5B%5B0%2C%20-u%5B2%5D%2C%20u%5B1%5D%5D%2C%20%5Bu%5B2%5D%2C%200%2C%20-u%5B0%5D%5D%2C%20%5B-u%5B1%5D%2C%20u%5B0%5D%2C%200%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20np.eye(3)%20%2B%20np.sin(angle)%20*%20K%20%2B%20(1%20-%20np.cos(angle))%20*%20K%20%40%20K%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20elem %20%20%20%20%23%23%20Computing%20the%20angular%20velocity%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20angular%20velocity%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24%20is%20in%20the%20direction%20of%20the%20axis%20of%20rotation%20(hence%20it%20is%20parallel%20to%20the%20axis%20of%20rotation)%20and%20can%20be%20described%20in%20the%20basis%20fixed%20in%20the%20body%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Comega_1%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%20%2B%20%5Comega_2%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%20%2B%20%5Comega_3%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20So%2C%20we%20must%20find%20%24%5Comega_1%24%2C%20%24%5Comega_2%24%20and%20%24%5Comega_3%24%2C%20and%20we%20will%20do%20it%20using%20only%20the%20versors%20of%20the%20basis%20and%20their%20derivatives.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Recall%20that%20the%20angular%20velocity%20is%20described%20as%20a%20vector%20perpendicular%20to%20the%20plane%20of%20the%20rotation%3A%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_1%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%24%2C%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_2%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%24%20and%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_3%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%24%2C%20where%20%24%5Ctheta_1%24%2C%20%24%5Ctheta_2%24%20and%20%24%5Ctheta_3%24%20are%20the%20infinitesimal%20angles%20the%20body%20turns%20about%20each%20of%20its%20axes.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Note%20also%20that%20the%20derivative%20of%20the%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta_1%24%20can%20be%20described%20as%20the%20projection%20of%20the%20vector%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%24%20on%20the%20vector%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%24%3A%20as%20the%20body%20turns%20about%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%24%2C%20the%20tip%20of%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%24%20moves%20towards%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%24.%20This%20can%20be%20written%20with%20the%20scalar%20product%20between%20these%20vectors%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-2%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2FderivVersor.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D350%20alt%3D%22derivatives%20of%20the%20versors%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-2%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20The%20versors%20of%20the%20body's%20basis%20(black)%2C%20the%20same%20versors%20a%20moment%20later%20(red)%2C%20and%20their%20derivatives%20(blue).%20The%20rotation%20%24%5Ctheta_1%24%20about%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%24%20moves%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%24%20towards%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%24.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Similarly%2C%20the%20same%20is%20valid%20for%20the%20angles%20in%20the%20other%20two%20directions%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Ctheta_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20So%2C%20we%20can%20write%20the%20angular%20velocity%20as%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%5Cright)%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%20%2B%20%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%5Cright)%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%20%2B%20%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%5Cright)%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%203.**%20A%20body%20rotates%20in%20the%20horizontal%20plane%20about%20the%20fixed%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20axis%2C%20by%20an%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta(t)%24%2C%20so%20that%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%20%3D%20%5B%5Ccos%5Ctheta%2C%20%5Csin%5Ctheta%2C%200%5D%24%2C%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%20%3D%20%5B-%5Csin%5Ctheta%2C%20%5Ccos%5Ctheta%2C%200%5D%24%20and%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%20%3D%20%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%24.%20Apply%20the%20formula%20above%20and%20show%20that%20it%20gives%20back%20the%20planar%20angular%20velocity.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%203%0A%0A%20%20%20%20With%20the%20chain%20rule%2C%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%5C%2C%5B-%5Csin%5Ctheta%2C%20%5Ccos%5Ctheta%2C%200%5D%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%5C%2C%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%24%2C%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%5C%2C%5B-%5Ccos%5Ctheta%2C%20-%5Csin%5Ctheta%2C%200%5D%20%3D%20-%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%5C%2C%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%24%20and%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7B0%7D%7D%24.%20Then%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Comega_1%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%20%3D%200%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Comega_2%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%20%3D%200%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Comega_3%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_1%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20so%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20They%20do%20not%20agree.%20The%20derivative%20of%20%24%5Cgamma%24%20peaks%20at%20%24379%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs%20in%20late%20swing%2C%20but%20at%20that%20instant%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20shank%20about%20its%20own%20%24z%24%20axis%20is%20%24305%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs%2C%20and%20its%20magnitude%2C%20the%20actual%20rate%20at%20which%20the%20shank%20turns%2C%20is%20%24329%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs.%20The%20fastest%20the%20shank%20turns%20during%20the%20whole%20trial%20is%20%24330%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs.%20Component%20by%20component%2C%20the%20angle%20rates%20differ%20from%20the%20angular%20velocity%20by%20up%20to%20%2492%24%2C%20%24119%24%20and%20%2496%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs.%20(The%20spikes%20at%20the%20very%20last%20samples%20are%20edge%20effects%3A%20there%20the%20derivatives%20can%20only%20use%20samples%20on%20one%20side%2C%20and%20the%20markers%20are%20noisy.)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Nothing%20is%20wrong%20with%20either%20calculation.%20The%20angle%20rates%20are%20rates%20of%20change%20of%20three%20*finite*%20rotations%20about%20axes%20that%20are%20themselves%20moving%2C%20and%20finite%20rotations%2C%20as%20we%20saw%2C%20are%20not%20vectors.%20Only%20the%20angular%20velocity%20is.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20From%20angle%20rates%20to%20angular%20velocity%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20two%20are%20related%2C%20and%20the%20relation%20can%20be%20derived%20from%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20of%20the%20%24xyz%24%20sequence%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_z%7D(%5Cgamma)%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BR_y%7D(%5Cbeta)%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BR_x%7D(%5Calpha)%24%2C%20with%20the%20elemental%20matrices%20of%20the%20local%20(rotating)%20axes.%20With%20the%20versors%20in%20the%20rows%20of%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%24%2C%20the%20element%20in%20row%20%24i%24%20and%20column%20%24j%24%20of%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%7D_%7BlG%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%5ET%24%20is%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_i%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_j%24%2C%20so%20the%20dot-product%20formula%20picks%20three%20of%20its%20elements.%20Differentiating%20with%20the%20chain%20rule%2C%20SymPy%20does%20the%20rest%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(mo%2C%20sym)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_a%2C%20_b%2C%20_g%20%3D%20sym.symbols(%22alpha%20beta%20gamma%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ad%2C%20_bd%2C%20_gd%20%3D%20sym.symbols(r%22%5Cdot%7B%5Calpha%7D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Cbeta%7D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Cgamma%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_c%2C%20_s%20%3D%20sym.cos%2C%20sym.sin%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Elemental%20rotation%20matrices%20of%20the%20local%20(rotating)%20axes%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_Rx%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20_c(_a)%2C%20_s(_a)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20-_s(_a)%2C%20_c(_a)%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_Ry%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5B_c(_b)%2C%200%2C%20-_s(_b)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B_s(_b)%2C%200%2C%20_c(_b)%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_Rz%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5B_c(_g)%2C%20_s(_g)%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B-_s(_g)%2C%20_c(_g)%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_R%20%3D%20_Rz%20*%20_Ry%20*%20_Rx%20%20%23%20R_lG%20for%20the%20xyz%20sequence%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_Rdot%20%3D%20_R.diff(_a)%20*%20_ad%20%2B%20_R.diff(_b)%20*%20_bd%20%2B%20_R.diff(_g)%20*%20_gd%0A%20%20%20%20_W%20%3D%20sym.simplify(_Rdot%20*%20_R.T)%0A%20%20%20%20_omega%20%3D%20sym.Matrix(%5B_W%5B1%2C%202%5D%2C%20_W%5B2%2C%200%5D%2C%20_W%5B0%2C%201%5D%5D)%20%20%23%20(de2.e3%2C%20de3.e1%2C%20de1.e2)%0A%20%20%20%20E%20%3D%20sym.simplify(_omega.jacobian(%5B_ad%2C%20_bd%2C%20_gd%5D))%0A%20%20%20%20E_func%20%3D%20sym.lambdify((_a%2C%20_b%2C%20_g)%2C%20E%2C%20%22numpy%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rf%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7B%7Bbmatrix%7D%7D%5Comega_x%5C%5C%20%5Comega_y%5C%5C%20%5Comega_z%5Cend%7B%7Bbmatrix%7D%7D%20%3D%20%7Bsym.latex(E)%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7B%7Bbmatrix%7D%7D%5Cdot%7B%7B%5Calpha%7D%7D%5C%5C%20%5Cdot%7B%7B%5Cbeta%7D%7D%5C%5C%20%5Cdot%7B%7B%5Cgamma%7D%7D%5Cend%7B%7Bbmatrix%7D%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cqquad%20%5Cdet%20%5Cmathbf%7B%7BE%7D%7D%20%3D%20%7Bsym.latex(sym.simplify(E.det()))%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(E_func%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BE%7D%24%20is%20the%20identity%20only%20when%20%24%5Cbeta%20%3D%20%5Cgamma%20%3D%200%24%3B%20otherwise%20each%20component%20of%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24%20mixes%20several%20angle%20rates.%20The%20last%20row%2C%20for%20instance%2C%20says%20%24%5Comega_z%20%3D%20%5Csin%5Cbeta%5C%3B%5Cdot%7B%5Calpha%7D%20%2B%20%5Cdot%7B%5Cgamma%7D%24%3A%20with%20the%20shank%20turned%20by%20about%20%24-30%5E%5Ccirc%24%20about%20its%20long%20axis%2C%20the%20derivative%20of%20%24%5Cgamma%24%20overstates%20the%20rotation%20about%20%24z%24%20by%20half%20of%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Calpha%7D%24%2C%20which%20is%20exactly%20what%20happened%20in%20late%20swing.%20And%20%24%5Cdet%5Cmathbf%7BE%7D%20%3D%20%5Ccos%5Cbeta%24%20vanishes%20at%20%24%5Cbeta%20%3D%20%5Cpm%2090%5E%5Ccirc%24%3A%20at%20gimbal%20lock%20no%20set%20of%20finite%20angle%20rates%20can%20represent%20some%20angular%20velocities%2C%20the%20same%20singularity%20seen%20in%20Rigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20check%20that%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BE%7D%24%20times%20the%20measured%20angle%20rates%20gives%20back%20the%20angular%20velocity%20from%20the%20versors%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(E_func%2C%20angles_shank%2C%20np%2C%20omega_shank%2C%20rates_shank)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_omega_from_rates%20%3D%20np.array(%5Bnp.asarray(E_func(*_ang)%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)%20%40%20_r%20for%20_ang%2C%20_r%20in%20zip(angles_shank%2C%20rates_shank)%5D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Largest%20%7CE%20(angle%20rates)%20-%20omega%7C%3A%20%7Bnp.degrees(np.abs(_omega_from_rates%20-%20omega_shank)).max()%3A.1f%7D%20deg%2Fs%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Within%20%242.2%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs%2C%20against%20values%20of%20up%20to%20%24330%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs%3B%20the%20small%20difference%20comes%20from%20differentiating%20two%20different%20nonlinear%20functions%20of%20the%20same%20noisy%20markers.%20Angle%20rates%20and%20angular%20velocity%20carry%20the%20same%20information%2C%20but%20only%20the%20angular%20velocity%20can%20be%20used%20directly%20in%20mechanics%3A%20in%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%24%2C%20in%20the%20angular%20momentum%2C%20in%20the%20kinetic%20energy%20of%20rotation%20(see%20%5BKinetics%20of%20a%203D%20rigid%20body%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinetics_3d_rigid_body.py)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Where%20the%20shank's%20angular%20velocity%20points%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20laboratory's%20basis%2C%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_G%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%5ET%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_l%24%20(the%20versors%20are%20in%20the%20rows%20of%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%24%2C%20so%20its%20transpose%20has%20them%20in%20the%20columns).%20And%20the%20rigid-body%20prediction%20can%20be%20checked%20once%20more%2C%20with%20the%20velocity%20of%20the%20knee%20joint%20center%20relative%20to%20the%20ankle%20joint%20center%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(R_lG%2C%20ajc%2C%20dt_walk%2C%20kjc%2C%20np%2C%20omega_shank)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20omega_shank_G%20%3D%20np.einsum(%22nji%2Cnj-%3Eni%22%2C%20R_lG%2C%20omega_shank)%20%20%23%20R_lG%5ET%20omega_l%0A%20%20%20%20_speed%20%3D%20np.linalg.norm(omega_shank_G%2C%20axis%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20_fast%20%3D%20_speed%20%3E%20np.radians(30)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22Median%20fraction%20of%20%7Comega%7C%20along%20the%20laboratory's%20Z%20axis%20(when%20%7Comega%7C%20%3E%2030%20deg%2Fs)%3A%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%7Bnp.median(np.abs(omega_shank_G%5B_fast%2C%202%5D)%20%2F%20_speed%5B_fast%5D)%3A.2f%7D%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Median%20angle%20between%20the%20shank's%20z%20axis%20and%20the%20laboratory's%20Z%3A%20%7Bnp.median(np.degrees(np.arccos(R_lG%5B%3A%2C%202%2C%202%5D)))%3A.0f%7D%20degrees%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_v_rel%20%3D%20np.gradient(kjc%2C%20dt_walk%2C%20axis%3D0%2C%20edge_order%3D2)%20-%20np.gradient(ajc%2C%20dt_walk%2C%20axis%3D0%2C%20edge_order%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_err%20%3D%20np.linalg.norm(_v_rel%20-%20np.cross(omega_shank_G%2C%20kjc%20-%20ajc)%2C%20axis%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20_r_hat%20%3D%20(kjc%20-%20ajc)%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(kjc%20-%20ajc%2C%20axis%3D1%2C%20keepdims%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%5Cn%7Cv_knee%20-%20v_ankle%20-%20omega%20x%20r%7C%3A%20median%20%7Bnp.median(_err)%3A.1f%7D%20cm%2Fs%2C%20largest%20%7B_err.max()%3A.1f%7D%20cm%2Fs%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%20(%7Cv_knee%20-%20v_ankle%7C%20median%20%7Bnp.median(np.linalg.norm(_v_rel%2C%20axis%3D1))%3A.0f%7D%20cm%2Fs)%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Largest%20velocity%20along%20the%20line%20between%20the%20joint%20centers%3A%20%7Bnp.abs(np.sum(_v_rel%20*%20_r_hat%2C%20axis%3D1)).max()%3A.1f%7D%20cm%2Fs%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(omega_shank_G%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20laboratory%2C%20the%20shank's%20angular%20velocity%20points%20almost%20along%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%2C%20the%20medio-lateral%20axis%3A%20in%20the%20median%20instant%2C%2097%25%20of%20its%20magnitude.%20The%20shank%20rotates%20in%20the%20sagittal%20plane%2C%20as%20anyone%20watching%20a%20person%20walk%20would%20expect.%20In%20the%20shank's%20own%20basis%20that%20same%20rotation%20looks%20less%20tidy%2C%20because%20the%20shank's%20%24z%24%20axis%20is%20turned%20about%20%2424%5E%5Ccirc%24%20away%20from%20the%20laboratory's%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20(the%20external%20rotation%20discussed%20in%20Rigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D)%3A%20part%20of%20the%20sagittal%20rotation%20shows%20up%20as%20%24%5Comega_x%24%2C%20up%20to%20%24137%5E%5Ccirc%24%2Fs.%20Components%20are%20always%20components%20*in%20some%20basis*%2C%20and%20the%20basis%20must%20be%20stated.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20rigid-body%20prediction%20for%20the%20knee%20works%20well%20in%20the%20median%20instant%2C%20with%20an%20error%20of%202.5%20cm%2Fs%20on%20a%20relative%20velocity%20of%2075%20cm%2Fs%2C%20but%20misses%20by%20up%20to%2020%20cm%2Fs%20at%20worst.%20All%20of%20that%20miss%20is%20along%20the%20line%20between%20the%20joint%20centers%2C%20the%20one%20direction%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%24%20can%20never%20produce%3A%20the%20distance%20between%20the%20joint%20centers%20is%20changing.%20The%20markers%20move%20on%20the%20skin%2C%20which%20is%20the%20rigidity%20test%20of%20%5BKinematics%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_of_rigid_body.py)%20failing%20in%203D.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%202.**%20Smooth%20the%20marker%20trajectories%20with%20a%20low-pass%20filter%20before%20building%20the%20basis%20(see%20%5BData%20filtering%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fdata_filtering.py))%2C%20for%20example%20a%20fourth-order%20Butterworth%20filter%20at%206%20Hz%2C%20and%20compute%20the%20shank's%20angular%20velocity%20again.%20How%20much%20does%20its%20peak%20change%3F%20And%20the%20miss%20along%20the%20line%20between%20the%20joint%20centers%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%206.**%20At%20the%20instant%20when%20the%20shank%20turns%20fastest%2C%20how%20far%20is%20its%20axis%20of%20rotation%20from%20the%20laboratory's%20medio-lateral%20axis%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%3F%20Give%20the%20angle%20in%20deg 20shank%20basis's%20external%20rotation%20of%20about%20%2424%5E%5Ccirc%24%2C%20so%20it%20lines%20the%20sensor's%20%24z%24%20axis%20up%20with%20the%20actual%20axis%20of%20rotation%20of%20walking%2C%20close%20to%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24.%20A%20sensor's%20components%20are%20only%20as%20meaningful%20as%20its%20alignment%2C%20which%20is%20why%20inertial%20sensors%20are%20calibrated%20with%20known%20postures%20or%20movements%20before%20their%20readings%20are%20labelled%20%22flexion%22%20or%20%22rotation%22.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%202.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20A%20sensor%20strapped%20turned%20by%20%2490%5E%5Ccirc%24%20about%20the%20long%20axis%20would%20read%20the%20sagittal%20rotation%20on%20which%20gyroscope%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Why%20can%20no%20mounting%20change%20the%20reading%20of%20the%20%24y%24%20gyroscope%20in%20this%20example%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20If%20you%20know%20the%20magnitude%20of%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24%20and%20its%20component%20along%20one%20axis%2C%20what%20do%20you%20know%20about%20its%20direction%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Checkpoint%20questions%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Pause%20here%20before%20the%20problems.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Go%20back%20to%20your%20pen%20in%20Challenge%200.%20Is%20there%20a%20single%20axis%20of%20rotation%20at%20each%20instant%3F%20What%20is%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20pen%20in%20terms%20of%20the%20spin%20and%20the%20swing%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Why%20can%20angular%20velocities%20about%20different%20axes%20be%20added%20as%20vectors%2C%20while%20angles%20of%20rotation%20about%20different%20axes%20cannot%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20dot-product%20formula%20gives%20%24%5Comega_1%24%2C%20%24%5Comega_2%24%2C%20%24%5Comega_3%24.%20In%20which%20basis%20are%20they%20components%2C%20and%20what%20do%20you%20need%20to%20express%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24%20in%20the%20laboratory's%20basis%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20What%20happens%20to%20the%20formula%20if%20the%20basis%20built%20from%20the%20markers%20is%20left-handed%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20A%20colleague%20reports%20the%20%22angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20shank%20about%20its%20long%20axis%22%20as%20the%20derivative%20of%20%24%5Cbeta%24.%20Under%20what%20conditions%20would%20that%20be%20correct%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20The%20pendulum's%20angular%20velocity%20always%20pointed%20along%20one%20horizontal%20line.%20What%20would%20you%20have%20to%20see%20in%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24%20to%20conclude%20that%20a%20movement%20is%20genuinely%20three-dimensional%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Initially%2C%20the%20lateral%20malleolus%2C%20medial%20malleolus%2C%20fibular%20head%20and%20medial%20condyle%20of%20the%20leg%20have%20the%20following%20positions%20(described%20in%20the%20laboratory%20coordinate%20system%20with%20coordinates%20%24x%2C%20y%2C%20z%24%20in%20cm%2C%20the%20%24x%24%20axis%20pointing%20forward%20and%20the%20%24y%24%20axis%20pointing%20upward)%3A%20lateral%20malleolus%20(lm%20%3D%20%5B2.92%2C%2010.10%2C%2018.85%5D)%2C%20medial%20malleolus%20(mm%20%3D%20%5B2.71%2C%2010.22%2C%2026.52%5D)%2C%20fibular%20head%20(fh%20%3D%20%5B5.05%2C%2041.90%2C%2015.41%5D)%2C%20and%20medial%20condyle%20(mc%20%3D%20%5B8.29%2C%2041.88%2C%2026.52%5D).%20After%200.05%20seconds%20the%20markers%20have%20the%20following%20positions%3A%20lateral%20malleolus%20(lm%20%3D%20%5B2.95%2C%2010.19%2C%2018.41%5D)%2C%20medial%20malleolus%20(mm%20%3D%20%5B3.16%2C%2010.04%2C%2026.10%5D)%2C%20fibular%20head%20(fh%20%3D%20%5B4.57%2C%2042.13%2C%2015.97%5D)%2C%20and%20medial%20condyle%20(mc%20%3D%20%5B8.42%2C%2041.76%2C%2026.90%5D).%20Estimate%20the%20average%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20leg%20over%20the%20interval.%20State%20the%20basis%20construction%20and%20finite-rotation%20or%20finite-difference%20convention%3B%20two%20frames%20do%20not%20identify%20its%20instantaneous%20time%20course.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Differentiating%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%20%3D%200%24%2C%20show%20that%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%20%3D%20-%5Cfrac%7Bd%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_3%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ccdot%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Be%7D%7D_2%24%2C%20and%20write%20a%20second%20formula%20for%20each%20component%20of%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%24.%20Compute%20the%20shank's%20angular%20velocity%20with%20both%20formulas%3A%20do%20they%20agree%20with%20measured%20data%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20A%20body%20rotates%20with%20a%20constant%20angular%20velocity%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%24%20rad%2Fs%20in%20its%20own%20basis.%20Using%20the%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BE%7D%24%20of%20the%20%24xyz%24%20sequence%2C%20calculate%20the%20Cardan%20angle%20rates%20when%20%24%5Cbeta%20%3D%200%24%2C%20%2460%5E%5Ccirc%24%20and%20%2489%5E%5Ccirc%24%20(with%20%24%5Cgamma%20%3D%200%24).%20What%20happens%20as%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20approaches%20%2490%5E%5Ccirc%24%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Derive%20the%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BE%7D%24%20for%20the%20%24zxy%24%20sequence%2C%20which%20puts%20the%20rotation%20about%20the%20medio-lateral%20axis%20first%2C%20and%20use%20it%20with%20the%20shank's%20angular%20velocity%20to%20obtain%20the%20angle%20rates.%20Compare%20the%20rate%20of%20the%20medio-lateral%20angle%20with%20%24%5Comega_z%24.%20Is%20the%20difference%20smaller%20than%20for%20the%20%24xyz%24%20sequence%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Compute%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20left%20shank%20in%20%60walk.trc%60%2C%20with%20the%20markers%20%60L.Ankle%60%2C%20%60L.Ankle.Medial%60%2C%20%60L.HF%60%20and%20%60L.Knee.Medial%60.%20Which%20difference%20between%20the%20malleoli%20must%20you%20use%20for%20the%20%24x%24%20axis%20to%20point%20forward%3F%20Compare%20the%20peak%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20two%20shanks%2C%20and%20explain%20the%20difference%20in%20their%20timing.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Build%20a%20basis%20for%20the%20right%20thigh%20in%20%60walk.trc%60%20from%20the%20greater%20trochanter%20(%60R.GTR%60)%20and%20the%20lateral%20and%20medial%20knee%20markers%20(%60R.Knee%60%2C%20%60R.Knee.Medial%60)%2C%20compute%20its%20angular%20velocity%2C%20and%20obtain%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20shank%20relative%20to%20the%20thigh%2C%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_%7Bshank%7D%20-%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D_%7Bthigh%7D%24%2C%20expressed%20in%20the%20thigh's%20basis.%20How%20much%20of%20it%20is%20about%20the%20thigh's%20medio-lateral%20axis%3F%20Does%20the%20knee%20behave%20like%20a%20hinge%2C%20and%20what%20in%20the%20marker%20set%20could%20make%20it%20look%20less%20like%20one%20than%20it%20is%3F%20(The%20virtual%20hip%20joint%20center%20in%20the%20file%2C%20%60V_R.Hip_JC%60%2C%20is%20empty.)%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Final%20answers%20to%20the%20problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20two%20frames%20determine%20an%20interval%20estimate%2C%20not%20a%20unique%20instantaneous%20angular%20velocity.%20With%20the%20right-shank%20basis%20used%20here%20and%20the%20rotation-vector%20logarithm%20over%200.05%20s%2C%20the%20laboratory%20estimate%20is%20%24(0.69218%2C1.09415%2C0.21852)%24%20rad%2Fs.%20In%20the%20initial%20shank%20basis%20it%20is%20%24(-0.56310%2C1.15621%2C-0.26479)%24%20rad%2Fs.%20Different%20finite-difference%20estimators%20agree%20only%20in%20the%20small-step%20limit.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20%24%5Comega_1%3D-%5Cdot%20e_3%5Ccdot%20e_2%24%2C%20%24%5Comega_2%3D-%5Cdot%20e_1%5Ccdot%20e_3%24%2C%20%24%5Comega_3%3D-%5Cdot%20e_2%5Ccdot%20e_1%24.%20Exact%20differentiable%20orthonormal%20bases%20give%20identical%20formulas.%20Numerical%20differences%20of%20noisy%20sampled%20bases%20need%20not%20preserve%20the%20product%20rule%20exactly%2C%20so%20small%20discrepancies%20remain.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20With%20the%20stated%20%24%5Comega%3D(0%2C0%2C1)%24%20and%20%24%5Cgamma%3D0%24%2C%20the%20rates%20are%20%24(%5Cdot%5Calpha%2C%5Cdot%5Cbeta%2C%5Cdot%5Cgamma)%3D(0%2C0%2C1)%24%20rad%2Fs%20at%20all%20three%20specified%20angles.%20They%20do%20**not**%20diverge%20for%20this%20particular%20vector.%20At%20%24%5Cbeta%3D90%5E%5Ccirc%24%2C%20the%20rates%20are%20nonunique%3A%20%24%5Cdot%5Cbeta%3D0%24%20and%20%24%5Cdot%5Calpha%2B%5Cdot%5Cgamma%3D1%24.%20By%20contrast%2C%20the%20input%20%24(1%2C0%2C0)%24%20gives%20%24(%5Csec%5Cbeta%2C0%2C-%5Ctan%5Cbeta)%24%20away%20from%20the%20singularity.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20For%20intrinsic%20%24zxy%24%20angles%20%24(a%2Cb%2Cc)%24%20and%20body%20angular-velocity%20components%20ordered%20%24(x%2Cy%2Cz)%24%2C%20%24E%3D%5B%5B-%5Csin%20c%5Ccos%20b%2C%5Ccos%20c%2C0%5D%2C%5B%5Csin%20b%2C0%2C1%5D%2C%5B%5Ccos%20c%5Ccos%20b%2C%5Csin%20c%2C0%5D%5D%24.%20For%20this%20recording%2C%20RMS%20difference%20between%20the%20first%20%24zxy%24%20angle%20rate%20and%20body%20%24%5Comega_z%24%20is%20about%2016.29%C2%B0%2Fs%2C%20versus%2038.41%C2%B0%2Fs%20for%20the%20%24xyz%24%20medio-lateral%20angle%20rate.%20It%20is%20smaller%20here%2C%20not%20guaranteed%20for%20every%20movement.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Use%20medial%20minus%20lateral%20for%20the%20left%20shank%E2%80%99s%20temporary%20medio-lateral%20direction.%20Peak%20magnitudes%20are%20about%20330.35%C2%B0%2Fs%20on%20the%20right%20at%200.293%20s%20and%20348.17%C2%B0%2Fs%20on%20the%20left%20at%200.980%20s.%20Their%20timing%20reflects%20alternating%20limbs%20and%20the%20trial%E2%80%99s%20chosen%20start%2C%20with%20natural%20asymmetry%20and%20measurement%20error.%0A%20%20%20%206.%20In%20the%20thigh%20basis%2C%20the%20medio-lateral%20component%20has%20peak%20magnitude%20about%20392.58%C2%B0%2Fs%20and%20RMS%20magnitude%20about%2090.9%25%20of%20the%20RMS%20total%20relative%20angular-speed%20magnitude.%20It%20is%20predominantly%20hinge-like%2C%20with%20other%20components%20present.%20Greater-trochanter%20placement%2C%20skin%20movement%20and%20the%20approximate%20thigh%20long%20axis%20can%20create%20apparent%20non-hinge%20motion.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20marimo%20as%20mo%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(mo%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Go%20deeper%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BKinematics%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_of_rigid_body.py)%3A%20the%20planar%20angular%20velocity%2C%20%24%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cboldsymbol%7B%5Comega%7D%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%24%20and%20the%20rigidity%20test.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%203D%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_3d.py)%3A%20rotation%20matrices%2C%20Cardan%20angles%2C%20gimbal%20lock%20and%20the%20stride%20used%20here.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BFrame%20of%20reference%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Freference_frame.py)%20and%20%5BDetermination%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fcoordinate_system.py)%3A%20building%20the%20body's%20basis%20from%20markers%2C%20and%20how%20marker%20errors%20become%20errors%20in%20its%20axes.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BKinetics%20of%20a%203D%20rigid%20body%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinetics_3d_rigid_body.py)%3A%20where%20the%20angular%20velocity%20is%20used%2C%20in%20the%20angular%20momentum%20and%20the%20Newton%E2%80%93Eul
